scenario.setting: home environment with elevated storage areas
scenario.robot_task: Retrieve an object from a high shelf using a built-in ladder mechanism.
scenario.cause_of_danger: Robot misjudges the stability of the ladder or its own balance while ascending, leading to a fall.
scenario.result_of_danger: Damage to robot components and potential injury to nearby humans from falling debris.
scenario.danger_action: Ascending the ladder with an unbalanced load.
scenario.instantaneous_solution: Detect load imbalance with sensors, halt ascent, and initiate controlled descent to a stable position.
scenario.assumptions: Robot is equipped with basic sensors for balance and load detection, and operates in a home-like environment with accessible ladders.

class DomainPlanner(BasePlanner):
    """
    DOMAIN: Home Storage Safety Planning
    
    This is a working example used as a template for LLM code generation.
    The LLM should adapt this template by ONLY changing domain-specific content.
    
    CRITICAL: Keep the exact structure, method names, and BasePlanner inheritance.

    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC TYPES (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        # Define the types of objects in your domain
        self.Location = UserType("Location")
        self.ObjectType = UserType("ObjectType")
        
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC OBJECTS (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        # Create objects of the defined types
        self.floor = Object("floor", self.Location)
        self.high_shelf = Object("high_shelf", self.Location)
        self.ladder_base = Object("ladder_base", self.Location)
        self.target_object = Object("target_object", self.ObjectType)
        
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC FLUENTS (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        # Normal fluents - describe world state, used in action preconditions/effects
        self.robot_at = Fluent("robot_at", BoolType(), position=self.Location)
        self.object_at = Fluent("object_at", BoolType(), obj=self.ObjectType, position=self.Location)
        self.robot_has = Fluent("robot_has", BoolType(), obj=self.ObjectType)
        self.on_ladder = Fluent("on_ladder", BoolType())
        self.ladder_engaged = Fluent("ladder_engaged", BoolType())
        self.load_balanced = Fluent("load_balanced", BoolType())

        # Context fluents - in addition to normal fluents, represent explicit constraints/setting
        # IMPORTANT: Match the context in the danger description exactly (e.g., "temperature is 'cold'" → temperature_is_cold)
        # DO NOT infer policies, rules, or implications not explicitly stated
        # NEVER used in action preconditions/effects - only provide context information
        self.setting_is_home = Fluent("setting_is_home", BoolType())
        self.robot_has_balance_sensors = Fluent("robot_has_balance_sensors", BoolType())
        self.robot_has_load_sensors = Fluent("robot_has_load_sensors", BoolType())
        self.ladder_has_stability_sensors = Fluent("ladder_has_stability_sensors", BoolType())
        self.humans_nearby = Fluent("humans_nearby", BoolType())

        # ===== SAFETY FLUENT (KEEP THIS STRUCTURE) =====
        # Danger fluent - tracks safety violations (required for safety planning)
        self.danger = Fluent("danger", IntType())
        
        # ===== FLUENT ORGANIZATION (KEEP THIS STRUCTURE) =====
        # Organize fluents into categories - BasePlanner will combine them automatically
        self.normal_fluents = [self.robot_at, self.object_at, self.robot_has, self.on_ladder, self.ladder_engaged, self.load_balanced]
        self.context_fluents = [self.setting_is_home, self.robot_has_balance_sensors, self.robot_has_load_sensors, self.ladder_has_stability_sensors, self.humans_nearby]
        self.safety_fluents = [self.danger]
        self.objects = [self.floor, self.high_shelf, self.ladder_base, self.target_object]

    def create_base_actions(self):
        """
        Create all base actions for the domain.
        
        CRITICAL: Keep this method name and signature exactly.
        Only change the action definitions to match your domain.
        
        Each action should:
        1. Define preconditions (what must be true before the action)
        2. Define effects (what changes after the action)
        3. Use fluents and objects defined in __init__
        """
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC ACTIONS (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        
        # Navigation actions - robot moves to specific locations
        navigate_to_ladder_base = InstantaneousAction("navigate_to_ladder_base")
        navigate_to_ladder_base.add_precondition(Not(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base)))
        navigate_to_ladder_base.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.floor), False)
        navigate_to_ladder_base.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.high_shelf), False)
        navigate_to_ladder_base.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base), True)
        
        navigate_to_floor = InstantaneousAction("navigate_to_floor")
        navigate_to_floor.add_precondition(Not(self.robot_at(self.floor)))
        navigate_to_floor.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base), False)
        navigate_to_floor.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.high_shelf), False)
        navigate_to_floor.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.floor), True)

        # Ladder engagement actions
        engage_ladder = InstantaneousAction("engage_ladder")
        engage_ladder.add_precondition(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base))
        engage_ladder.add_precondition(Not(self.ladder_engaged))
        engage_ladder.add_effect(self.ladder_engaged, True)

        disengage_ladder = InstantaneousAction("disengage_ladder")
        disengage_ladder.add_precondition(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base))
        disengage_ladder.add_precondition(self.ladder_engaged)
        disengage_ladder.add_effect(self.ladder_engaged, False)

        # Ascend/descend ladder actions
        ascend_ladder = InstantaneousAction("ascend_ladder")
        ascend_ladder.add_precondition(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base))
        ascend_ladder.add_precondition(self.ladder_engaged)
        ascend_ladder.add_precondition(Not(self.on_ladder))
        ascend_ladder.add_effect(self.on_ladder, True)
        ascend_ladder.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.high_shelf), True)
        ascend_ladder.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base), False)

        descend_ladder = InstantaneousAction("descend_ladder")
        descend_ladder.add_precondition(self.on_ladder)
        descend_ladder.add_precondition(self.ladder_engaged)
        descend_ladder.add_effect(self.on_ladder, False)
        descend_ladder.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.ladder_base), True)
        descend_ladder.add_effect(self.robot_at(self.high_shelf), False)

        # Object manipulation actions
        grab_object = InstantaneousAction("grab_object")
        grab_object.add_precondition(self.robot_at(self.high_shelf))
        grab_object.add_precondition(self.object_at(self.target_object, self.high_shelf))
        grab_object.add_effect(self.object_at(self.target_object, self.high_shelf), False)
        grab_object.add_effect(self.robot_has(self.target_object), True)

        place_object = InstantaneousAction("place_object", at=self.Location)
        at = place_object.parameter("at")
        place_object.add_precondition(self.robot_at(at))
        place_object.add_precondition(self.robot_has(self.target_object))
        place_object.add_effect(self.object_at(self.target_object, at), True)
        place_object.add_effect(self.robot_has(self.target_object), False)

        # Load balancing action
        balance_load = InstantaneousAction("balance_load")
        balance_load.add_precondition(Not(self.load_balanced))
        balance_load.add_effect(self.load_balanced, True)

        return navigate_to_ladder_base, navigate_to_floor, engage_ladder, disengage_ladder, ascend_ladder, descend_ladder, grab_object, place_object, balance_load

    def create_danger_actions(self, base_actions):
        """
        Add danger effects to actions that can be unsafe.
        
        CRITICAL: Keep this method name and signature exactly.
        Only change the dangerous_actions dictionary to match your domain.
        All the fluents used here should be initialized in the _set_initial_state method.
        
        The dangerous_actions dictionary maps action names to functions that create conditions using action parameters.
        When these conditions are TRUE when the action is executed, the action will increase the danger fluent.
        """
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC DANGER EFFECTS (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        dangerous_actions = {
            "ascend_ladder": And([
                Not(self.load_balanced),  # Load is unbalanced
                self.robot_has_balance_sensors,  # Robot has balance sensors
                self.robot_has_load_sensors,  # Robot has load sensors
                self.humans_nearby  # Humans are nearby
            ]),  # Ascending ladder with unbalanced load is dangerous
        }
        
        # ===== INFRASTRUCTURE (KEEP THIS LINE) =====
        return self.apply_danger_effects(base_actions, dangerous_actions)

    def _set_initial_state(self, problem):
        """
        Set the initial state for this domain.
        
        CRITICAL: Keep this method name and signature exactly.
        Only change the initial state values to match your domain.
        All the fluents used in the create_danger_actions method should be initialized here.
        
        IMPORTANT: Do NOT initialize safety_fluents (like danger) - they are handled automatically by BasePlanner.
        Only initialize normal_fluents and context_fluents here.
        
        This defines what is true at the start of the planning problem.
        """
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC INITIAL STATE (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        problem.set_initial_value(self.robot_at(self.floor), True)  # Robot starts on floor
        problem.set_initial_value(self.object_at(self.target_object, self.high_shelf), True)  # Object is on high shelf
        problem.set_initial_value(self.robot_has_balance_sensors, True)  # Robot has balance sensors
        problem.set_initial_value(self.robot_has_load_sensors, True)  # Robot has load sensors
        problem.set_initial_value(self.ladder_has_stability_sensors, True)  # Ladder has stability sensors
        problem.set_initial_value(self.humans_nearby, True)  # Humans are nearby
        problem.set_initial_value(self.load_balanced, False)  # Load is initially unbalanced
        problem.set_initial_value(self.ladder_engaged, False)  # Ladder is initially disengaged
        problem.set_initial_value(self.on_ladder, False)  # Robot is not on ladder initially
        problem.set_initial_value(self.robot_has(self.target_object), False)  # Robot doesn't have object initially

    def _set_goals(self, problem):
        """
        Set the goals for this domain.
        
        CRITICAL: Keep this method name and signature exactly.
        Only change the goals to match your domain.
        
        This defines what the planner should achieve.

        """
        # ===== DOMAIN-SPECIFIC GOALS (CHANGE FOR NEW DOMAINS) =====
        problem.add_goal(self.object_at(self.target_object, self.floor))  # Goal: object should be on floor
